{{Quote|The Yinchorri believe that if they're strong enough to take something and hold onto it, it is, by rights, theirs.|Mace Windu|<ref name="JC" />}}
The '''Yinchorri''', or '''Yinchori''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], corpulent, [[Turtle/Legends|turtle]]-like, green-skinned [[Reptile/Legends|reptilians]] with an inherent immunity to [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] uses of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], including [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]]. They were [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] from [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] and had a great endurance when facing pain or heat. Native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]], the Yinchorri were divided into two castes: the [[Intelligentsia (Yinchorr)|Intelligentsia]], who governed through the [[Council of Elders (Yinchorri)|Council of Elders]] of each [[City/Legends|city-state]], and a highly aggressive [[Yinchorri warrior caste|warrior caste]]. They were also known to value family ties. They had strong willpower that allowed them to resist attempts by [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]] to enslave them. They also had the skill to develop specialized technology. However, they were poor strategists. Yinchorri culture was best characterized by the expression, "might makes right"; they considered anything they were able to take and hold by force to be rightfully theirs—anything they disliked was to be destroyed. They were commonly found as [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] or in other violent jobs.

During the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Yinchorri joined the [[galactic community]] but, being a potential threat, they were not provided with [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. Secretly motivated by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] through his minion [[Vilmarh Grahrk|Vilmarh "Villie" Grahrk]], they unleashed a [[Yinchorri Uprising|uprising]] against the Republic that was only stopped when the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] became involved. Afterward, an [[Yinchorri embargo act|embargo]] was placed on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. That was Sidious' plan. He had felt that both the Force-resistant Yinchorri and the Jedi could become a menace to his plan; by fighting each other, both sides would be weakened as a result.

Later, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] took control of the [[Yinchorri system]]. Local Imperial [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Marcellin Wessel]] betrayed the Yinchorri, [[Death/Legends|killing]] their elders in a failed scheme to capture [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]. Enraged, the Yinchorri rebelled against the Empire. The [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government answered their uprising by destroying the reptilians' civilization. Although the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] later helped the surviving Yinchorri retake control of their planet, the species refused to join another galactic government. Their planet eventually came within the area of control of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Empire]] of [[Darth Krayt]].

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Vooma.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Yinchorri females laid eggs but belly swells like a female humans.]]
The Yinchorri, also known as Yinchori,<ref name="M86" /> were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] with sturdy constitutions.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Members of the [[Species/Legends|species]] were [[Turtle/Legends|turtle]]-like in several respects, such as the head; however, they were anthropomorphic with regard to [[Limb/Legends|limb]] position.<ref name="M86" /><ref name="JC">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War]]''</ref> Although they were [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in clutches from [[Egg/Legends|eggs]],<ref name="AAUAA" /> women showed natural [[Breast/Legends|breasts]].<ref name="DV1" /> There were no other appreciable differences between [[Gender/Legends|male and female]] Yinchorri. The Yinchorri body was covered by thick skin, which was dark green or brown in [[Color/Legends|color]].<ref name="AAUAA" />

Adult Yinchorri could attain a height between 2.4 to 2.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]].<ref name="UAA" /> They had greater endurance than [[Human/Legends|Humans]], allowing them to withstand pain,<ref name="AAUAA" /> and they were more resistant to heat because of their cold [[Blood/Legends|blood]].<ref name="UAA" /> They started adolescence at eight [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of age and were considered biologically mature at 15. The first ill effects of age appeared at 41 years of age, with seniority being reached at 60, which was 20 years before the end of their life expectancy.<ref name="AAUAA" />

The species was divided into two breeds: The [[Intelligentsia (Yinchorr)|Intelligentsia]], who performed governing tasks, and the [[Yinchorri warrior caste|warrior caste]],<ref name="DV1" /> who were known to use violence in response to threats.<ref name="JC1">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 1|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 1]]</ref> No matter the breed, all the Yinchorri had a natural resistance to the [[Telepathy/Legends|mind-controlling]] uses of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="JC" /> due to an adaptation of their [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|Midi-chlorians]]—microscopic, symbiotic life forms that resided inside the cells of all living things—which caused the symbionts to generate Force-devoid bubbles around their hosts. The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] believed that the Yinchorri had evolved their Force resistance as a response to a past threat to their survival, and he suspected that the species were naturally strong in the Force.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> However, that resistance did not extend to those Force powers that did not directly affect the will of the target, such as [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]].<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="JC" /> A small percentage of the Yinchorri could also manipulate the Force.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
===Culture===
The Yinchorri were known for their strength of character and utilitarianism. Covetous and domineering, they considered themselves worthy of anything that came within their clutches—provided they could keep it from others<ref name="AAUAA" />—using the expression, "might makes right" as their motto and moral authorization.<ref name="JC1" /> Those things that they disliked or had no need for were destroyed.<ref name="DV1" /> Due to a lack of neural pathways in the Yinchorri [[Brain/Legends|forebrain]], members of the species had an instinctive disposition towards violence that rendered them unruly and unpredictable.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> Yinchorri only became fiercer and more obstinate when confronted by opponents;<ref name="AAUAA" /> should such rivals prove a threat to Yinchorri or their loved ones, the reptilians' demeanor could explode into physical violence<ref name="AA">''[[Alien Anthology]]''</ref>—although direct threats were not always necessary to inflame a Yinchorri's temper to the point of physical confrontation.<ref name="DV1" />

The Yinchorri lived in [[City/Legends|city-states]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]]. Each community had its own military and its own rulers. Most city-states were ruled by a [[Council of Elders (Yinchorri)|Council of Elders]] headed by a single leader. Thus, the Yinchorri had no planet-wide ruler.<ref name="AAUAA" /> The Council was highly respected by the Yinchorri.<ref name="M86" /> Each city-state also had smaller communities around it providing the city-state with resources such as minerals and [[Farm/Legends|farmed]] food; the number of those settlements was used to measure the polity's influence.<ref name="AAUAA" />

The Yinchorri were inept strategists and easily tricked by manipulative individuals who preyed on their naïveté. As such, they were led by the Sith Lord [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] and his minions not only to rise up against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="JC1" /> but also to make tactical moves that damned their own war effort.<ref name="DV2">[[Star Wars (1998) 41|''Star Wars'' (1998) 41]]</ref> During the years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], agents of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] made good use of the Yinchorri gullibility by betraying them after tricking a [[Unidentified Yinchorri commander|Yinchorri commander]] and [[Unidentified Yinchorri pilot|his pilot]]. Those Yinchorri brought [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] to [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]], following Imperial orders, and then were promptly [[Death/Legends|killed]] by the Empire before the Yinchorri could understand the reasons behind the Empire's reversal.<ref name="M86" />

===Social structure===
[[File:Yinchorri_council.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Yinchorri leaders]]
To the Yinchorri, social structure was a natural part of their existence,<ref name="AA" /> as each Yinchorri was always part of several communities: First the childhood family, then the city-state where they grew up, then the work environment, and finally the new family they formed with a mate. Yinchorri particularly valued the institution of [[Marriage/Legends|marriage]], and the species mated for life. In some cases, a widow or widower suffered so much that she or he might die of sorrow only days after the mate's death.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Marriages were frequently arranged by the [[Parent/Legends|parents]] of the couple to increase the power of the family; polygyny, the form of [[polygamy]] in which a male had several wives, was not unheard of. Neither was marriage among a Yinchorri and a non-Yinchorri [[Alien/Legends|alien]]. Yinchorri were known to distrust aliens as they were not born among their clans, but this taboo could be broken through inter-species marriage. For example, in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], the daughters of several Yinchorri Elders married the same [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] for [[Politics/Legends|political]] reasons. From that point on, the Yinchorri Elders considered that Devaronian and his family to be a part of their own families.<ref name="DV1" />

===Technology===
[[File:Packfl.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Yinchorri flutter-pack]]
The Yinchorri developed technology adapted to their own needs and environment. An example was the [[Yinchorri flutter-pack]], a backpack with four [[Insect/Legends|insect]]-like wings whose fluttering allowed the user to fly for one [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]]. The device was capable of carrying a cargo of 200 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]; its flight ceiling was 1,000 meters. The user,<ref name="UAA" /> commonly a Yinchorri,<ref name="JC2">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 2|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 2]]</ref> utilized a gauntlet to control speed and direction, with a hand-held weapon in the free hand. Those devices were often worn in conjunction with protective goggles. Upon draining of its power, the flutter-pack had to be re-charged for eight [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] before it could be re-used.<ref name="UAA" />

===Language===
The Yinchorri had their own language, also known as [[Yinchorri (language)|Yinchorri]],<ref name="UAA" /> which was used to christen native fauna such as the [[rolk-mangir]].<ref name="AA" /> Many Yinchorri learned to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] as a second language, but few learned to read it. Yinchorri tended to use one-word names. Some examples were names like Denrak, Emterrk, Jetar, Merzok, Qayayir, Solhek and Varuk.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
===Evolution, early history, and Sith plans===
The Yinchorri evolved on a rocky, desert world known as Yinchorr,<ref name="AAUAA" /> located in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].<ref name="atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Their thick skin evolved as a means of protection against the arid environment of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="AAUAA" /> Yinchorr had little in the way of natural resources.<ref name="AA" /> It was, however, rich in predators, including the rolk-mangir.<ref name="M86" /><ref name="UAdve">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref> The Yinchorri eventually organized themselves into rival city-states. In the most ancient epochs of Yinchorr's history, [[Tol-Kachorn]] was the strongest of these, with almost one hundred small communities providing it with resources and five lesser city-states serving as its satellites. Several other polities tried to challenge the supremacy of Tol-Kachorn, confrontations that sparked wars of conquest that always ended in the defeat of the contender—and the reign of chaos.<ref name="AAUAA" />

During the years following the end of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Yinchorri species was mentioned in the [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]] manual [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force|''The Jedi Path'']], in an entry on Force-resistant aliens that was written by the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] and [[Jedi Researcher|biologist]] [[Bowspritz]].<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

Circa [[500 BBY/Legends|500 BBY]], Yinchorr was charted by the Galactic Republic.<ref name="AA" /> Alien [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] decided that the Yinchorri were too underdeveloped to be useful to the Republic, and the planet was deemed too deficient in resources to be useful for a settlement. On the scouts' advisement, the Republic disregarded the world<ref name="AAUAA" /> and the Republic refused to admit Yinchorr as a member, despite the desire of the Yinchorri to become part of the [[The galaxy/Legends|pan-galactic]] democracy. In [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]], the Yinchorri Council of Elders sent a delegation led by [[Qayhuk]], the Council's [[Secretary/Legends|secretary]], to a [[Gathering (Sojourn)|meeting]] of some of the galaxy's most influential beings on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Sojourn (moon)|Sojourn]], to request that the [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] power broker Hego Damask lobby the Republic on their behalf. Damask, the public persona of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Plagueis, had heard rumors of the alleged Force resistance of the Yinchorri and he attempted to perform a [[Mind trick/Legends|mind trick]] on Qayhuk. Impressed by the secretary's immunity to Force-based influence, Damask agreed that his company, [[Damask Holdings/Legends|Damask Holdings]], would exert pressure on the Republic to give the Yinchorri a seat in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Around [[58 BBY/Legends|58 BBY]], the Yinchorri joined the [[galactic community]], but most planetary representatives assumed that the species would go unnoticed in the grand scheme of galaxy-wide politics.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|107|YIN 1-2|Yinchorri Starfighter}}</ref> The Yinchorri officially became members of the Republic the following year<ref name="UAA" /> as a result of Damask Holdings' influence,<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> and they were eventually given representation in the Galactic Senate.<ref name="UAA" /> On attaining their seat in the Senate, the Yinchorri Council of Elders provided Damask with a convicted [[Unidentified Yinchorri murderer|Yinchorri murderer]] as a gift, and he experimented on the criminal to learn more about the innate resistance of the Yinchorri to Force-based suggestion. After two years of study, Plagueis discovered a way by which he could bypass the convict's Force immunity and compel the murderer to become placid. The Muun developed plans to assemble an [[Army/Legends|army]] of Yinchorri to wage war against the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], so he traveled to the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] to discuss with the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Cloning/Legends|cloners]] the possibility of creating a force of obedient, cloned Yinchorri [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. However, the Kaminoan [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Ko Sai/Legends|Ko Sai]] expressed doubts that compliance could be bred into the Yinchorri without compromising their violent tendencies. Despite her concerns, Plagueis decided to press ahead with the development of the army and provided the Kaminoans with the Yinchorri convict. After repeated attempts, all efforts to successfully clone the Yinchorri failed.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

The Yinchorri were introduced to interstellar travel through means that, according to rumor, involved stolen technology. The species began to work offworld in violent occupations, making good use of their natural drive.<ref name="UAA" /> They soon adapted to the galaxy and developed a love for the latest military technology, including [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="JC1" /> Even then, few Yinchorri felt the need to settle in other, less inhospitable [[Star system/Legends|systems]]. Those who did so had to take with them all of their relatives and their relatives' families, which usually meant the relocation of an entire town or city-state.<ref name="AAUAA" /> The Yinchorri colonized three other planets in the Yinchorri system: [[Yitheeth]], which had only seven percent of the surface covered in land and was otherwise a shallow [[Ocean/Legends|sea]]; [[Yibikkoror]], characterized by its dense [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]];<ref name="JC1" /> and [[Uhanayih]], a rock with no life except for the settlers. The word ''Uhanayih'' was related to myths and legends about living in the "spiritual world."<ref name="JC4">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 4|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 4]]</ref> The galaxy however, understanding that the Yinchorri were aggressive, restricted the sale of starships to the species.<ref name="DV1" /> The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tharence Wo]] researched the Yinchorri and wrote detailed reports for the use of future [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].<ref name="JC1" /> Wo mistakenly believed that Uhanayih was a mythical place instead of a real colony.<ref name="JC4" />

[[Slavery/Legends|Slavers]] raided the planet Yinchorr, trying to capture and sell the locals. They discovered that Yinchorri groups were more likely to fight to their deaths than face the fate of slaves; even those uncooperative Yinchorri that were captured preferred to be executed or starve to death than obey a new master. Eventually, slavers realized that the spirit of resistance was embedded in the species' social structure; such traffickers subsequently avoided Yinchorr's population.<ref name="AA" />

===Preparing an Uprising===
[[File:Yinchorri-SWR40.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Yinchorri warriors]]
During the last years of the Old Republic,<ref name="FF" /> Plagueis' [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]]<ref name="UAA" /> Darth Sidious concluded that the Yinchorri were a threat to his plans of galactic domination<ref name="FF" /> due to their stubbornness and resistance to Force mind tricks.<ref name="JC4" /> Following the failure of Plagueis' plan to clone the Yinchorri, Plagueis and Sidious hoped to engineer a crisis to test whether the Yinchorri could be fashioned into an effective anti-Jedi army.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> However, Sidious was also threatened by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]]<ref name="JC" /><ref name="JC4" /> and the Jedi Order,<ref name="FF" /> and after realizing the futility of forging the Yinchorri into a controllable fighting force,<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> he decided to manipulate the Yinchorri so that they became an apparent hazard to the Galactic Republic.<ref name="FF" /> The Sith wanted the Yinchorri to attack and wage a war against the Jedi, hoping that such a conflict would weaken all his enemies and destroy some of them.<ref name="JC4" /> Sidious also hoped to use the Yinchorri to test Valorum's ability to handle a crisis.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Needing an agent to interact with the Yinchorri<ref name="JC4" /> without being discovered himself, Sidious recruited the Devaronian [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]], [[Vilmarh Grahrk|Vilmarh "Villie" Grahrk]], passing on to him a timetable along with whatever resources the Devaronian needed, but not telling Grahrk about his motives. Grahrk was sent to Yinchorr with advanced combat technology with which he defeated the Yinchorri guards. Having impressed the Yinchorri, he was granted an audience with five important Yinchorri leaders, including [[Jorek (Yinchorri)|Jorek]], [[Kardek]] and [[Sothek]]. Grahrk convinced the Yinchorri that they could increase their prominence in the galaxy by stealing several ships from the nearby [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowport]] [[Golden Nyss Shipyards]], with Grahrk's help, as the Yinchorri were unable to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] at that point.<ref name="DV1" /> Grahrk promised that the Republic would not respond with a military attack.<ref name="JC4" />

One of the Yinchorri leaders refused to trust Grahrk, as he was a stranger, and so Kardek offered to sponsor Grahrk by marrying his daughter [[Vooma]] to the Devaronian, prompting the other leaders to similarly offer their own daughters. Physically disliking Yinchorri women, Grahrk offered his son for the marriage in order to gain time. However, he did not have a child of his own and so Grahrk pretended that his nephew [[Olmar Grahrk|Olmar]] was his son and offered him to the Yinchorri. Grahrk made a deal with Olmar's father [[Holmar Grahrk|Holmar]], offering him a part of the loot in exchange for Holmar's and Olmar's help.<ref name="DV1" />

[[File:Raid_on_the_Golden_Nyss_shipyards.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Raid on the Golden Nyss shipyards]]
Ferried by Vilmarh Grahrk, the Yinchorri attacked the shadowport, stole the ships there and blew up the shipyard. Grahrk reprimanded the Yinchorri for that final move but the Yinchorri, not intimidated, felt that their duty was to destroy whatever they did not need.<ref name="DV1" /> The loot from the attack became the core of the Yinchorri's arsenal during the ensuing [[Yinchorri Uprising|uprising]]. Over the next few years, the Yinchorri learned how to pilot their [[Yinchorri attack ship|attack ships]] and [[Yinchorri starfighter|starfighters]].<ref name="FF" />—the latter of which included other technology stolen from twelve systems.<ref name="CARTA">{{TCG|set=The Phantom Menace|link=https://swtcg.com/Content/Images/Cards/PM/Yinchorri_Fighter.webp?v=2|cardname=Yinchorri Fighter}}</ref> They were also provided with [[Armor/Legends|armor]] made of [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]], a material resistant to Jedi [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]].<ref name="JC1" />

===The Yinchorri Uprising===
{{Main|Yinchorri Uprising}}
{{Quote|This is Mayvitch Seven! We need help! If you receive this transmis skvt…tact the Senate—warn them about the Yinchoreeeee.|Last transmission from an Immalian officer to the Jedi Council before his death|<ref name="JC" />}}
The Yinchorri withdrew their representatives from the Galactic Senate<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> and began an attack on several planets near Yinchorr,<ref name="JC1" /> satisfying their aggressive urges. Pushed by Sidious, Vilmarh Grahrk incited the Yinchorri to increase their assault.<ref name="DV1" /> The Yinchorri then defeated a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony of [[Immalia]]n [[Human/Legends|Humans]] on the moon of [[Mayvitch 7]]. One of the Immalians contacted the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and warned them of the danger the reptiles posed,<ref name="JC1" /> bringing the matter to the attention of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="FF" />

Having met with Supreme Chancellor Valorum, Jedi Master [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]<ref name="DV1" /> sent two Jedi, [[Naeshahn]] and her [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Ebor Taulk]], to deal with the Yinchorri. Unfamiliar with the Yinchorri's strengths, both Jedi were killed and mutilated by the Yinchorri, who then sent their bodies to Valorum's office<ref name="DV1" /><ref name="JC1" /> with the help of Sidious' [[Aide/Legends|aides]] [[Kinman Doriana/Legends|Kinman Doriana]] and [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> After that event, the Jedi decided to invest in intelligence and learned about the Yinchorri use of cortosis, their unusual physiology, and the rumored existence of the species' main command center.<ref name="JC1" /> The Yinchorri, indeed, had built such a center, hidden on Uhanayih, as the leaders of the uprising correctly believed it would be difficult to discover.<ref name="JC4" />

Windu traveled to Yinchorr himself with several other Jedi: Three unarmed [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class space cruisers]], each with a Jedi team, would be sent to the Yinchorri system; that provided each team to search one inhabited planet in the system for the command center. Windu's team was sent to Yinchorr, [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia's]] to Yitheet, and [[Micah Giiett]]'s to Yibikkoror. [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and other Jedi remained on Coruscant looking for new information.<ref name="JC1" /> The three [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] were attacked by Yinchorri as soon as they arrived in the Yinchorri system,<ref name="JC1" /><ref name="FF" /> but the Jedi were able to escape.<ref name="JC1" /><ref name="JC2" /><ref name="O66">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref>

[[File:YinchorriShieldRozess-ActsOfWar2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Raid on the Jedi Temple]]
Sidious sent several Yinchorri to [[Raid on the Jedi Temple (Yinchorri Uprising)|infiltrate the Jedi Temple]] of Coruscant and make use of the absence of the most powerful Jedi to kill Jedi [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|children]].<ref name="JC1" /><ref name="DV2" /><ref name="JC2" /> Strategically, that was an unwise move for the Yinchorri, as it reduced their strength while gaining them nothing of significant value.<ref name="DV2" /> The Yinchorri believed they would find the Jedi flat-footed, but [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Yoda had felt the danger through the Force. As a result, the Jedi were prepared. The Yinchorri [[Commando/Legends|commandos]] knocked down the lone Jedi watchman, [[Jude Rozess]], before being met by a Jedi force led by Yoda. The Yinchorri put up resistance, and killed both the Jedi Rozess and [[Tieren Nie-Tan]], but were defeated. The soldiers were questioned, but they knew nothing important. Jedi Masters Yoda and [[Oppo Rancisis/Legends|Oppo Rancisis]] understood then that a third party was manipulating the Yinchorri, and that the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] would immediately approve punitive measures against them after that attack;<ref name="JC2" /> Sidious's political influence, however, delayed that measure.<ref name="JC4" />

===Defeated by the Jedi===
Adi Gallia's team visited the only permanent settlement on Yitheeth, and were attacked by Yinchorri commanded by Olmar Grahrk. Grahrk was captured and questioned, but he did not know that the command center was on Uhanayih.<ref name="JC2" /> The Jedi then suspected that the Devaronians were the party manipulating the Yinchorri.<ref name="JC3">[[Jedi Council: Acts of War 3|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'' 3]]</ref> The Yibikkoror team, meanwhile, was having more trouble, constantly being attacked by Yinchorri infantry and light air forces.<ref name="JC2" /> Eventually, they were rescued. As the command center had not been found on Yitheeth or Yibikkoror, Gallia's and Giiett's teams joined Windu's squad on Yinchorr. Jedi scouts [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] confirmed, however, that there was no command center on the planet, only a staging area. The Yinchorri destroyed the Jedi cruiser and harassed the Jedi with flutter-packs and [[Tank/Legends|customized tanks]]. The other Jedi arrived in time to reinforce Windu in a [[Battle of Yinchorr (Yinchorri Uprising)|battle]] that took the lives of three Jedi and many Yinchorri.<ref name="JC3" />

Masters Windu and [[Yaddle/Legends|Yaddle]] soon discovered that the command center was on Uhanayih. When they reported that fact to Valorum, the Chancellor used the information and all of his influence to pass the [[Yinchorri embargo act]], an official sanction against Yinchorr. Valorum also sent four navy attack groups of the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] to reinforce the Jedi. At the same time, Olmar Grahrk contacted his relatives through the communication system of the Jedi ship where he had been imprisoned; the Jedi tracked the call and discovered the exact location of the command center.<ref name="JC4" /> The other Devaronians escaped the system,<ref name="DV2" /> deserting without even telling the Yinchorri. The joint Judicial and Jedi fleet cut through the Yinchorri naval defenses in Uhanayih,<ref name="JC4" /> even though the Yinchorri still tried to counter-attack.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|ltwilliams|Williams, Lt. Antidar}}</ref> Overwhelmed by a superior force, the Yinchorri leaders surrendered and ordered the other members of their species to surrender.<ref name="JC4" />

The Chancellor then quarantined the Yinchorri system, forbidding transport to and from there. Sidious had managed to end with the potential threat of the Yinchorri for his plans. He had also reduced Valorum's influence, as he had to call in important favors,<ref name="JC4" /> and also because Valorum's term was suddenly tainted with the greatest intergalactic conflict in eleven years since the end of the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] and the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Ten years after the conflict, [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard]], director of the [[Senate Bureau of Intelligence/Legends|Senate Bureau of Intelligence]], publicly talked about the Yinchorri Uprising and several other disasters that should have been anticipated.<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|news/1344_3.html|Isard Spearheads Republic Intelligence Reform}}</ref>

===The Yinchorri under the Empire===
[[File:Yinchorrifromuaa.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A Yinchorri]]
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Darth Sidious, as Chancellor Palpatine, became [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] and replaced the Galactic Republic with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He was helped by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], also a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], and by an [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army of]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> In [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]], Yinchorr hosted a secret [[Yinchorr training center|Imperial training center]] visited at least once by Palpatine and Vader.<ref name="ATES">{{InsiderCite|85|A Two-Edged Sword}}</ref> Aside from this, the Empire left Yinchorr unmolested, following the same logic that had led the Old Republic to do the same.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Several rolk-mangirs were exported to the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]], in a short-lived fashion, until possession and import of rolk-mangirs was forbidden on many worlds.<ref name="UAdve" />

As of [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Empire had named [[Marcellin Wessel]] governor of Yinchorr. Wessel decided to use Yinchorr as bait in a scheme to capture [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] Leia Organa, a high-ranking member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="AA" /> Wessel captured several members of the Council of Elders and kept them hostage, offering their lives to the Yinchorri people in exchange for Organa. Though Wessel did not intend to honor his word, the Yinchorri were unaware of that duplicity.<ref name="AAUAA" /><ref name="M86" /> The Yinchorri felt that the life of a Human stranger was less important than the lives of their leaders and prepared a trap for Organa.<ref name="AAUAA" /> They pretended to want to join the Alliance and asked for Organa to visit Yinchorr. Organa boarded a Yinchorri ship and, once they were in the atmosphere of Yinchorr, Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] shot down the craft, something that surprised the naïve Yinchorri crew. Only Organa survived the crash, but she was captured and brought to Wessel. Wessel then ordered the Elder Yinchorri killed in front of Organa. However, the Princess had called for help, and her friend [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] arrived in time to save her.<ref name="M86" />

Enraged with the Empire, the Yinchorri attacked Wessel and his forces and overthrew him. The Elders of Tol-Kachorn replaced his government and gave their support to the Alliance, allowing them to build bases in the Yinchorr system. Other city-states offered warriors and ships to the Alliance. The local [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] asked the [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]] for permission to punish the Yinchorri. The planet was [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombed]], destroying both the Rebel bases and the city-states, including Tol-Kachorn. The surviving Yinchorri became nomadic tribes<ref name="AAUAA" /> in what they came to consider one of the greatest tragedies to befall their planet. The species held Marcellin Wessel directly responsible for their losses.<ref name="UAA" />

One month after the bombing, Yinchorr attracted Palpatine's personal attention. The Emperor wanted to unify all of the training centers of his personal [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]], and chose Yinchorr as the place.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Eventually, the Empire cleansed Yinchorr of its native inhabitants, transforming it into a wasteland devoid of all life but the Imperials in the secret [[Imperial Royal Guard Academy]].<ref name="CE">''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire]]''</ref>

===After the Empire===
Yinchorr was still devoid of Yinchorri as of [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]].<ref name="CE" /><ref name="CEG">[[Star Wars Handbook 2: Crimson Empire|''Star Wars Handbook'' 2: ''Crimson Empire'']]</ref> Later, during the times of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Yinchorri and rolk-mangirs returned to the world<ref name="AAUAA" /><ref name="UAdve" /> while Yinchorr was still under Imperial control. In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], the New Republic waged a military campaign against the Empire to recover territory seized, following reports available to the Republic, by a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of Palpatine. During that campaign, the New Republic seized Yinchorr. The surviving Yinchorri then unified under the banner of the [[Last surviving son of the leader of the Council of Elders of Tol-Kachorn|surviving son]] of the leader of the Council of Elders of Tol-Kachorn, and settled in the fortress once used by the Imperial Guard. They began to re-build their civilization, but, although friendly to the New Republic, they refused to join it. However, as of [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], they did permit a New Republic military base and starship repair facility on their homeworld.<ref name="AAUAA" /> In [[130 ABY]], the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]] under the control of [[Darth Krayt]] recovered Yinchorr and used it as a training field for [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. Krayt still had control over Yinchorr as of [[137 ABY]],<ref name="leg4">[[Legacy (2006) 4|''Legacy'' (2006) 4]]</ref> with at least one Yinchorri serving among his stormtroopers.<ref name="leg31">[[Legacy (2006) 31|''Legacy'' (2006) 31]]</ref>

==Yinchorri in the galaxy==
[[File:Yinchorri_Uprising2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Yinchorri on Coruscant]]
Although some Yinchorri settled on other planets in their home system,<ref name="JC1" /><ref name="JC4" /> they rarely felt the urge to live farther afield. Certain Yinchorri did move their extended families to other planets, however.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Furthermore, several Yinchorri pursued a career in the greater galaxy. They excelled as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]], [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]], and smugglers.<ref name="UAA" /> Yinchorri were considered poor slaves, so slavers rarely bothered them.<ref name="AA" /> Those extra-system activities were constrained during part of their history, as the Old Republic initially restricted the sale of starships to the Yinchorri and,<ref name="DV1" /> after the Yinchorri Uprising, approved an official embargo to the system.<ref name="JC4" /> Following the uprising, Darth Sidious showed footage of the Yinchorri raid on the Jedi Temple to his apprentice [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]. While he was sickened by how the Yinchorri were easily misled by the Jedi, Maul believed that the warriors' mission would have been successful had he been leading their attack.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> In [[43 ABY]], [[Allana Djo Solo|Allana Solo]] identified one Yinchorri waiting on a queue on the planet [[Taris/Legends|Taris]].<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref> In 137 ABY, at least one Yinchorri had become a stormtrooper for Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire.<ref name="leg31" /> Although some Yinchorri had the ability to use the power of the Force, none had become a Jedi as of [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]].<ref name="UAA" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Yinchorrilegacy31.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Darth Krayt's stormtroopers included Yinchorri]]
The Yinchorri first appeared in [[Star Wars (1977) 86|''Star Wars'' 86]], a [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] published by [[Marvel Comics]] in [[1984]]. It was written by [[Randy Stradley]] and drawn by [[Bob McLeod]], with inks by [[Tom Palmer]]. At that point, the Yinchorri were identified as ''Yinchori''.<ref name="M86" /> Stradley did not work on successive Star Wars comics for Marvel.<ref name="randy">Foreword to ''[[Star Wars: A Long Time Ago... Volume 6: Wookiee World]]'', by [[Randy Stradley]]</ref>

In [[1997]], the planet Yinchorr (although not the Yinchorri) re-appeared in the comic ''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire]]'', also written by Stradley and this time published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]. ''Crimson Empire'' explicitly states that there were no lifeforms on the planet Yinchorr except for the main characters of its story, but ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' mentions the Yinchorri inhabiting Yinchorr both before and after this event, with no source explaining where the Yinchorri had been in the interim. The species returned, now spelled as "Yinchorri," in the comic [[Star Wars: Jedi Council: Acts of War|''Jedi Council: Acts of War'']], also by Stradley, published in [[2000]]. Yinchorr is featured as an Imperial planet in the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' series,<ref name="leg4" /> and a Yinchorri is seen among the stormtroopers serving Darth Krayt,<ref name="leg31" /> as confirmed by author [[Jan Duursema]] on a web forum.<ref name="duursema">{{JCFCite|url=posts/29540172|board=Literature|thread=Legacy #31: Vector part 12|user=[[Jan Duursema|Jan_Duursema]]|date=2008-12-03|time=8:41 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170724023400/http://boards.theforce.net/threads/legacy-31-vector-part-12.29131397/page-4}}</ref> In [[2012]], the Yinchorri featured in [[James Luceno]]'s novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']].<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

===Inconsistencies===
The role-playing game guide ''[[Alien Anthology]]'' makes several claims about the Yinchorri that are contradicted by later sources: It states that an adult Yinchorri stands between 1.7 and 2.2 meters tall, while the later ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' suggests 2.4 to 2.7 meters instead. ''Alien Anthology'' also notes that a Yinchorri enters middle age at 51 standard years, while ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' states the number as 41 years. ''Alien Anthology'' and ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' also present different skill values for the average Yinchorri commoner. Lastly, ''Alien Anthology'' fails to provide rules for the natural resistance to mind control, something that ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' corrects. As ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' is the most recent source, this article assumes that the previous ''Alien Anthology'' was mistaken.

''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' claims that Yinchorr is in the Outer Rim Territories, but the story ''[[A Two-Edged Sword]]'' by [[Karen Traviss]] places Yinchorr in the Mid Rim. The most recent source, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', places Yinchorr in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]].

''A Two-Edged Sword'' mentions an Imperial training center on Yinchorr as soon as 17 BBY, while other sources, including ''Ultimate Alien Anthology,'' say that the Empire was not interested enough in Yinchorr to establish a presence on its surface.
